newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Hewlett-Packard-Singapore JV worth over US$1.0 bln.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard-Singapore JV worth over US$1.0 bln.

text.p: The head of Singapore electronics maker Chartered Semiconductor Manufacturing, Tan Bock Seng, said on Thursday his company's joint venture with Hewlett-Packard was worth more than US$1 billion.
A joint venture source earlier told reporters the plant was worth more than Singapore $1 billion (US$694 million).
Tan told a news conference financial details of the venture, which will make Application Specific Integrated Circuits for the electronics industry, would not be disclosed.
But pressed by reporters to give a figure, Tan said:
"More than $1 billion." He made clear he meant U.S. dollars, not Singapore dollars.

Chartered Semiconductor will hold the majority of the shares in the joint venture, Chartered Silicon Partners Pte Ltd, with Hewlett-Packard and the Singapore government's Economic Development Board holding minority stakes.
Ground-breaking for the company's new factory is expected in September and production is projected to start in 1999.
The factory would have the capacity to produce more than 30,000 eight-inch wafers per month when fully operational, a company statement added.
Chartered Semiconductor is part of the state-owned Singapore Technologies conglomerate.
